title: fix(plugin-detail): read `relationshipValueField` off the typed schema, not through `as any`
body:
Fixes #9475

`record:related_list` now reads `relationshipValueField` off its typed `schema`
instead of through `(schema as any)`.

⚠️ **Type parameters are written with SQUARE brackets throughout this body**
(`Record[string, any]`), because the GitHub body sanitizer eats angle-bracket
shaped fragments — including inside backticks. The source says it the normal way.

## What the card asked for, and what the instrument answered

The card asserted the cast exists and deliberately asserted nothing about what
the read's type is: the expression instrument had never been pointed at this
site. It has now been, on `origin/main` `aced50d2e`:

| reading | before (2026-09-18T21:14:40Z) | after (2026-09-18T21:16:18Z) |
|---|---|---|
| `typeof` the read `relationshipValueField` | `any` | `string \| undefined` |
| CONTROL, same command: `typeof schema.columns` | `string[] \| undefined` | `string[] \| undefined` |

The control fires in the **same** command as the reading, so `any` is a reading
and not an artefact of an instrument that prints `any` for everything.
`getPropertyOfType` on the binding — the membership instrument — reported the
key as declared in **both** columns, which is exactly why the declaration looked
like it had arrived.

## ⭐ The corpus, since the card left it unmeasured

The card's own "Not measured" line asks whether other renderers carry the same
shape. Measured at `aced50d2e`, 2026-09-18T21:15:22Z, by resolving each
`(schema as X).KEY` read and asking whether the UN-cast `schema` type
**declares** `KEY` (`getPropertiesOfType`, which lists real members only, so a
key admitted by an index signature does not count):

- **14** renderer sources scanned · **22** `(schema as X).KEY` reads · **7** of
  them over a key the schema type declares.
- `record-related-list.tsx` — `relationshipValueField` (1, this card) and
  **`add` (4)**.
- `record-details.tsx` — **`hideFields` (2)**. That is objectui#8649's OTHER
  mirror alignment, inert at its own read site for the same reason. ⛔ Out of
  this card's fence; filed as a finding below.
- `record-highlights.tsx` — none.
- The other 15 reads are `requiredPermissions` / `enforceFieldSecurity` /
  `redactFields`, which no block of the contract declares — those casts are not
  this defect, and `detailRendererUndeclaredKeys-8649.test.ts` ledgers them.
  15 "no" beside 7 "YES" in one run is what makes the "no" column a reading.

## ⚠️ What this repair does NOT buy — measured, and the dispatch expected otherwise

The dispatch prescribed a misspelled key as the ablation input, "which the cast
accepts and the declared read must refuse". **The declared read does not refuse
it**, and that is a second finding rather than a detail. This renderer's own
`schema` type is not `RecordRelatedListComponentProps`; it is that interface
intersected with `Record[string, any]`, and an index signature admits any key at
`any`. One `tsc` pass, all four legs in the same command:

- misspelled key through the renderer's `schema` type → **no error**
- CONTROL, same command, same misspelling through the mirror interface (no index
  signature) → **TS2551**, "Did you mean `relationshipValueField`?"
- correct spelling assigned to `number` → **TS2322**

⇒ the repair moves the read from `any` to the declared type, so a wrong-TYPED
use of the correct spelling is now refused; a TYPO at this site still is not.
The declaration's refusal power stops one type layer earlier than the cast did.
Pinned as a live ledger leg in the new test with its control, so the day that
intersection is narrowed the limit is re-derived instead of outliving its subject.

## Runtime: inert, as the card suspected

The renderer already applied the contract's `.default('id')` itself (`|| 'id'`),
untouched here. Four render legs pin it: absent ⇒ the parent link value is the
record id; explicit `'id'` ⇒ the same; `'name'` ⇒ that field off the parent
record; `'name'` while the parent is still loading ⇒ `null`, i.e. no fetch.

And the published module does not move: `packages/plugin-detail/dist/index.js`
built from the re-cast tree and from the un-cast tree hash the **same**
`sha256:270d7ad84a4ff526b26217b5c236005e3a56e56ee1dc5bf9d61c476fce5d5849`, with
the second build's mtime proving it was a real rebuild and not a replayed cache.
That is why the changeset declares an empty frontmatter: nothing releases.

## Ablation — mutate, prove, run, restore, prove

Mutation: put `(schema as any)` back at the repaired read. Anchored on the exact
repaired text, with an anchor-miss made loud; restore is
`git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`, under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`.

- blob at `HEAD` and on disk before: `2a4a46c0275f16998879b07fc14e9d60f56ae89f`
- on disk after mutation: `e0e126178c0d789758bf58ca7a34df6782c22060` (differs ⇒ the mutation landed)
- anchor counts before → after: un-cast `1 → 0`, cast `0 → 1`
- **vitest, under the mutation: 2 failed | 7 passed.** The two that failed are
  the source-text guards — "reads `relationshipValueField` off `schema` UN-CAST"
  and "no cast stands between `schema` and ANY contract-declared key". The seven
  that passed include every runtime leg, which is the runtime-inertness reading
  above, taken rather than argued.
- **`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, under the mutation: exit 0 — GREEN.** ⭐ The
  honest negative, and it changed this pull request: my first draft called the
  type-level `Equal` leg "the card's claim as a compile-time assertion, RED
  before this card". It was not. An indexed access on the TYPE is a MEMBERSHIP
  question, and membership is what a cast leaves intact — the card's own lesson,
  repeated one layer up in its own pin. The leg is renamed
  `_SchemaTypeCarriesTheDeclaredMember` and labelled for what it does guard (the
  objectui#8649 annotation erasure). The discriminating leg in this file is the
  source-text one.
- restored blob: `2a4a46c0275f16998879b07fc14e9d60f56ae89f` (equal to `HEAD`) and
  `git diff HEAD` empty.

## The guard is derived, not a list

The new pin ranges over the keys the CONTRACT declares on `record:related_list`,
read off `RecordRelatedListProps.shape` every run, and asserts no cast stands
between `schema` and any of them. A key the platform declares tomorrow joins the
guard with nobody editing the file. The one exemption — `add` — is ledgered with
its measured reason and asserted STILL CAST, so it cannot outlive its subject.

## Acceptance notes

- **`add` is left cast, and the cast is load-bearing.** Measured: un-casting all
  four `add` reads yields exactly one `TS2322` — the mirror types
  `add.picker.filter` as `unknown` while `RelatedList`'s own prop types it as
  `ViewFilterRule[]`, and `unknown` is not assignable to that. Repairing it means
  moving one of those two declarations; `packages/types` is fenced off for this
  card (PR objectui#9895 holds 100 files there) and `RelatedList.tsx` is outside
  its surface. Filed as a finding, and ledgered in the new test meanwhile.
- **objectui#9593 is untouched.** That decision-box card is on the same file but
  on `columns`; nothing in this diff reads, moves or re-spells `columns`.
- `recordRelatedListInputs.spec-parity.test.ts` asserts the renderer source
  matches `relationshipValueField || 'id'`. It matched the cast form and the
  un-cast form alike — the same non-discriminating shape the card warns about —
  and still matches. Left alone: it is a different file's assertion about a
  different claim. Carrier: the next seat to touch that file.
- noted, not filed: the `|| 'id'` fallback folds an authored EMPTY STRING to
  `'id'`, while the contract's `z.string().default('id')` accepts `''` as a valid
  string. No reachable harm (an empty field name resolves nothing either way) and
  ⛔ not changed here. Carrier: none.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` — **189 files, 1861 tests, all passed**
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) — green
- `pnpm --filter "@object-ui/plugin-detail^..." build` — green (dependency closure, so the pins read a rebuilt `.d.ts`, not a cached one)
- gates: `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:published-tsconfig-exclude`, `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:handler-key-reads` — all exit 0; `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0 and names the empty frontmatter as the complete answer; `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` says NOT GOVERNED for all three paths.
- eslint, narrowed and declared: the two touched source files only, **2 files linted** by `--format json`, **0 errors**. The narrowing is safe to make because `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting — zero occurrences of `projectService` or `project:` in it, against 9 occurrences each of `rules:` and `files:` as the control — so no rule in this configuration can read a file my diff did not touch. The repository-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run, not this one's.
- NOT MEASURED: remote CI. This pull request is handed over before CI converges.
